title: Supply Chain Security: Image Scanning, Attestation and Admission Control, Trusted Sources and VM Patching

concepts.heading: Scanning Before Publication and Keeping Results Fresh
concepts.body: Artifact Analysis scans container images in two ways, and the stem's timing words choose between them. Automatic scanning runs when an image is pushed to Artifact Registry and then keeps the findings updated as new vulnerability data arrives, so it is detective: the image is already in the registry when the scan runs. On-Demand Scanning is started by a command, can scan an image stored locally without pushing it, and its results are available for up to 48 hours and are not updated afterward. To stop a vulnerable image from being published, add a Cloud Build step that runs On-Demand Scanning on the freshly built image, reads the severities and fails on HIGH or CRITICAL, so the push step never runs. Continuous updating has a catch: it continues only for images pulled within the last 30 days. After that the results go stale, and metadata stale for more than 90 days is archived and available only through the API. An eight-month-old image that nobody pulls and shows no new finding has not been proven clean, so rebuild and redeploy long-lived images in CI/CD.

concepts.heading: Binary Authorization: Attestors, Policies and Separation of Duties
concepts.body: Binary Authorization decides at deploy time whether an image may run. An attestation is a record, signed with a private key, stating that a specific image digest completed a stage such as QA or security review. An attestor is the resource that holds the matching public key and verifies those signatures. A rule in the require-attestations mode may list several attestors, and the image then needs attestations verified by all of them, so one attestor per approving team gives a logical AND. A policy has one default rule plus optional specific rules, which on GKE can target clusters, namespaces and Kubernetes service accounts. Put the strict requirement in the default rule and relax only the development cluster with a specific rule, so a cluster added later starts protected. Each project has exactly one policy, in the project where the platform runs. To stop a compromised CI service account from approving its own builds, use a multi-project setup: the deployment project holds only the policy, an attestor project holds the attestors and their verification keys, and an attestation project holds the records.

concepts.heading: Rolling Out and Operating Binary Authorization
concepts.body: Each rule has an evaluation mode (what is checked) and an enforcement mode (what happens on failure). Dry Run: Audit Log Only lets non-conformant images deploy but records them in Cloud Audit Logs, so a team can find unsigned pipelines before it switches to Block and Audit Log. Break-glass is the emergency path: a label on the Pod specification requests it, and every use is written to Cloud Audit Logs for review or alerting. A strict default can block GKE's own system Pods, which exempt image paths and trust of Google-maintained system images prevent. On Cloud Run only the default rule is supported, and the organization policy constraint run.allowedBinaryAuthorizationPolicies, set to the value default, requires enforcement in every project below it. A promoted copy of the same digest in another registry can reuse the attestation, but a rebuilt image has a new digest and needs a new one. Deploy-time checks do not flag running Pods. Continuous validation does monitor them, but its check-based form is Preview in the current documentation, so exam answers do not rely on it.

concepts.heading: Trusted Sources, Dependency Confusion and VM Patching
concepts.body: Controls on where artifacts come from sit beside image signing. The compute.trustedImageProjects organization policy limits which projects' images principals may use to create disks, but it does not restrict custom images in the local project, image files in Cloud Storage, or creating image resources locally, so a developer who can create images can still use them. Close that gap with IAM on image creation and detection. For packages, an Artifact Registry virtual repository fronts several upstream repositories of one format; higher priority values take precedence, equal priorities can be served from either, and leaving gaps lets you insert upstreams later. Dependency confusion happens when a public package shares an internal name, so rank the internal repository above the remote one. For VMs, VM Manager patch deployments install updates through the package manager and offer three reboot options: Default lets the agent decide, Always reboots, and Never does not, which in some cases leaves patches not fully applied. A scanner that still flags an old kernel after a successful run points to a reboot that never happened. The maintenance window limits when patching starts, not what runs afterward.

examPoints: A question that must stop a vulnerable image before it is pushed points to an On-Demand Scanning step in Cloud Build that fails on blocked severities, not to automatic scanning, which runs after the push.

A question that requires both QA and security approval, or approvals that a compromised CI account cannot forge, points to one attestor per team in a require-attestations rule, with the policy, attestors and attestations split across projects.

A question where a patch job reports success but the scanner still flags the old kernel points to the reboot option, and one that rolls out a new admission policy safely points to Dry Run: Audit Log Only before blocking.

quiz.q: A regulated company needs a production GKE cluster to run only images that the QA team and the application security team have each approved. Each team must keep its own signing key so that neither can forge the other's approval. Which Binary Authorization design fits?
choices: A default rule that requires attestations from two attestors, one per team, each with its team's public key
A default rule that lists a single attestor whose public key is shared by both teams for every signing operation
A default rule set to allow all images, with each team asking developers to avoid unapproved images by convention
A specific rule per namespace that requires one attestor, rotated between the two teams each release cycle
quiz.explain: When several attestors are listed in one rule, the image needs attestations verified by all of them, which gives a logical AND while each team keeps its own private key. A shared key lets either team forge the other's approval, allow-all enforces nothing, and one rotating attestor does not require both approvals.

quiz.q: A monthly VM Manager patch deployment for Linux VMs reports success, yet the vulnerability scanner flags the old kernel a day later. The deployment uses the reboot option Never. What is the most likely cause and fix?
choices: The maintenance window was too short, so the fix is a longer window that lets the patch job run beyond its end time
The scanner caches results for a month, so the fix is a tag change on the image to trigger a fresh scan
The kernel update needs a restart to take effect, so the fix is the Default or Always reboot option
The patch job does not cover kernels, so the fix is an organization policy that forces every VM to be replaced
quiz.explain: A new kernel typically takes effect only after a restart, and the Never option does not reboot, so patches can be left not fully applied. The maintenance window only limits when patching starts, retagging an image does not change a running VM, and an organization policy cannot replace VMs.

recap: Gate the build with On-Demand Scanning, require one attestor per approving team at deploy time with duties split across projects, roll out in dry run, and remember that patching, trusted sources and stale scans each leave their own gap.

title: Posture and Drift: Custom Organization Policies, Security Posture and Custom Detectors

concepts.heading: Preventing and Detecting: Custom Constraints and Custom Modules
concepts.body: Posture work separates stopping a bad state from finding one. An organization policy is preventative. A custom constraint is written in CEL for a resource type and a method such as create, and it allows or denies matching requests. Policy changes are usually not retroactive: if the policy restricts a state that a resource is already in, the resource is in violation but the service does not stop its behavior, to protect business continuity, and violations must be fixed manually. Suppose a new hardening setting is required on every GKE cluster and several existing clusters already violate it. A custom constraint stops new violations without disrupting the old clusters, and a detective control finds the old ones. Security Health Analytics custom modules are that detective control: they are defined in YAML with CEL expressions, target any resource that Security Command Center supports, and write findings to Security Command Center. Test an organization policy before enforcing it. Policy Simulator shows how it would affect resources, and dry-run mode logs violations without denying them. Custom module findings are not covered by attack path simulation, so they carry no attack exposure scores.

concepts.heading: The Security Posture Service and Drift
concepts.body: Security Command Center includes a security posture service to define, deploy and monitor a posture. A posture is one or more policy sets, and each holds policies that are preventative (organization policy constraints, including custom constraints) or detective (Security Health Analytics detectors, including custom modules). Predefined templates follow standards such as CIS, NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001 and PCI DSS, or Google-recommended settings. Essentials templates can be deployed without changes, while extended templates must be customized to match the environment first. A posture is deployed at an organization, folder or project, and only one posture can be deployed to each resource. Postures are inherited, and where a lower-level posture defines a policy differently, the lower-level definition is used below it, so the usual advice is a broad organization posture with stricter ones on production folders. After deployment, drift, an unauthorized change from the posture, is reported as Security Command Center findings that can be filtered and exported. The documentation says the service needs a paid Security Command Center tier activated at the organization level.

concepts.heading: Custom Detection Beyond the Predefined Detector
concepts.body: Predefined detectors are fixed, which is why a custom module exists. The predefined PUBLIC_SQL_INSTANCE detector flags a Cloud SQL instance whose authorized networks include 0.0.0.0/0. The documentation's example of a custom module matches address prefixes with wildcards, ignores instances in the MAINTENANCE state, or triggers only for specific regions. That is the answer when a stem needs a rule the predefined detector cannot express, and building a scheduled script that polls the API is the answer to avoid. Security Health Analytics checks the configuration of resources, so ask whether the signal is the state of a resource. Its detectors map to benchmark controls such as CIS, NIST, PCI-DSS and HIPAA. Event Threat Detection reads Cloud Logging and Google Workspace logs for events, and Virtual Machine Threat Detection scans VM instances for potentially malicious applications such as cryptocurrency mining software, so neither replaces a configuration check. Pairing a preventative constraint with a detective module for the same risk covers both new and existing resources.

concepts.heading: Guardrails with Gaps: Locations and Service Restriction
concepts.body: Two organization policy constraints are common guardrails, and each has documented limits. The resource locations constraint limits where new resources of supported services can be created. Resources created before the constraint continue to exist, global resources such as Compute Engine global addresses and resources with no location choice are not affected, some services are not enforced on sub-resource creation (Cloud Storage is one example), and a policy containing it is not a data storage commitment. Pair it with an inventory of existing resources and, for regulated scope, Assured Workloads monitoring. The Restrict Resource Service Usage constraint controls runtime access to all in-scope resources and applies to all access to all resources in scope, with eventual consistency, so a mistake is costly. It works in one of two mutually exclusive modes, a denylist or an allowlist, and it excludes essential dependencies such as IAM, Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring. Use tags to scope enforcement conditionally, start with a pilot set of resources and widen after observing the impact. A Resource Manager tag in a conditional organization policy rule scopes a constraint inside a folder.

examPoints: A question that must block new violations without disrupting existing clusters points to a custom constraint in an organization policy, paired with a Security Health Analytics custom module to find the old violations.

A question that wants one set of preventative and detective controls deployed, inherited and monitored for drift points to the security posture service in Security Command Center, with extended templates customized before use.
A question where an auditor finds a global resource or an old resource despite an enforced locations policy points to the constraint's documented limits, not to a failure of the policy.

quiz.q: A security team adopts a requirement that every new GKE cluster must have a specific hardening setting, while several existing clusters already violate it. The team wants to stop new violations without disrupting the existing clusters and still see the old violations. Which combination fits?
choices: A custom constraint that denies noncompliant cluster creation, plus a Security Health Analytics custom module
A weekly export of cluster configurations to a spreadsheet, plus an email that asks cluster owners to fix their settings
A custom constraint alone, because the policy retroactively reports every existing noncompliant cluster as a finding
A deny policy in IAM that removes the cluster admin role from every engineer until each cluster is fixed
quiz.explain: A custom constraint prevents new violations and does not stop the behavior of existing resources, because policy changes are generally not retroactive. A Security Health Analytics custom module is the detective control that writes findings for resources that already violate the rule. A manual export, a constraint on its own, or an IAM deny would leave a gap or cause disruption.

quiz.q: A platform team wants to deploy a broad set of organization policy constraints and Security Health Analytics detectors to the whole organization and stricter ones to the production folder, and be told when someone changes a setting. Which service fits?
choices: Policy Simulator, which previews a change but does not deploy policies or report later changes
The security posture service, which deploys inherited postures and reports drift as findings
Cloud Asset Inventory, which lists resources but does not evaluate or enforce any posture
Access Approval, which asks an approver to consent before Google staff may touch resources
quiz.explain: The security posture service defines postures made of preventative and detective policies, deploys them at the organization, folder or project level with inheritance, and reports unauthorized changes as drift findings. The other services preview, list or gate different things.

recap: Prevent with custom constraints, detect with Security Health Analytics custom modules, deploy and monitor both as a posture, and remember that policy is not retroactive and locations and service restriction have documented gaps.

title: Network Telemetry: Firewall Logs, VPC Flow Logs, Packet Mirroring, Cloud IDS and Observability Analytics

concepts.heading: Rule Logs Versus Flow Logs: Which Question Each Answers
concepts.body: Firewall policy rules logging and VPC Flow Logs are different telemetry for different questions. Rules logging writes a record when a connection is established and answers which rule allowed or denied it. A connection stays active while packets are exchanged at least once every 10 minutes, so a continuous stream produces one entry for its whole life, and only TCP and UDP connections are recorded. If logging is turned on for a rule that matches an already active connection, no new entry is generated until the connection has been idle for at least 10 minutes and a new packet is sent. VPC Flow Logs sample packets and aggregate them by 5-tuple over an aggregation interval, so a long-lived connection produces entries throughout, and they describe volume and timing for monitoring and forensics. Suppose responders suspect a VM holds one TCP connection to an external server for hours and moves data. Rules logging shows the single allow decision, while flow logs show the ongoing transfer. Neither records payload. Turn logging on before the activity you want to investigate.

concepts.heading: Flow Log Scope and the Short-Connection Blind Spot
concepts.body: Flow logs can be enabled at the organization, VPC network, subnet, VLAN attachment and Cloud VPN tunnel scopes, and at project level for specific networks, subnets, attachments or tunnels. An organization-level configuration enables flow logs for all subnets, VLAN attachments and Cloud VPN tunnels in all VPC networks in the organization, so resources created later are included, which fits a company that keeps creating projects. Logs go to Cloud Logging in the project of the VPC network that reported the flow and are stored for 30 days by default; keep them longer with a custom retention period or by exporting them. Sampling has a cost. The primary sampling rate is dynamic and cannot be adjusted, and an optional secondary rate applies after aggregation, so short-lived or low-volume TCP connections can be missed, which is exactly what a port scan produces. The optional TCP connection logging setting captures all outbound TCP connection attempts (the initial SYN) and all acknowledged inbound connections (the SYN-ACK reply) for VM instances and serverless endpoints, and it can be set for a subnet, a VPC network or an organization.

concepts.heading: Packet Mirroring and Cloud IDS
concepts.body: When flow metadata is not enough, Packet Mirroring clones the traffic of selected instances, including payloads and headers, and forwards it for examination. Sources are Compute Engine instances chosen by subnet, network tags or instance names, and the collector is an instance group behind an internal passthrough Network Load Balancer whose forwarding rule is enabled for mirroring. Filters limit the extra bandwidth that mirroring consumes on the VMs. All sources in one policy must be in the same project, VPC network and region, and the collector must be in that region too, so mirroring two regions needs two policies. Cloud IDS builds on mirrored traffic: an endpoint attached to a mirroring policy detects exploit attempts and spyware. Tune it with a minimum alert severity for the whole set, or with threat exceptions that disable specific threat IDs, limited to 99 per endpoint; one confirmed false positive is a threat exception, not a higher severity. Cloud NGFW Layer 7 inspection and a Cloud IDS endpoint must not apply to the same traffic, because the inspection policy takes priority and the traffic is not mirrored.

concepts.heading: Analyzing Network Logs: Observability Analytics and Field Access
concepts.body: Logs Explorer is for troubleshooting and exploration and does not support aggregate operations such as counting entries. Observability Analytics, previously called Log Analytics, runs SQL over log buckets that have been upgraded to use analytics, with grouping, aggregation, charting and joins of log and trace data. For the top talkers by hour across several months of flow logs, upgrade the bucket and query it, and create a linked BigQuery dataset when BigQuery needs to query the same data without ingesting a second copy. The bucket must be created at project level and unlocked, unless it is the _Required bucket, and logs written before the upgrade need a backfill that can take several days. Field-level access controls change the picture. A bucket can hide fields such as source IP addresses from some principals, but you cannot use the Observability Analytics page to query log views when the bucket has field-level access controls, and BigQuery does not honor them, so anyone who can query the linked dataset can read all fields. Grant the dataset only to people entitled to every field, or give restricted analysts another path such as Logs Explorer.

examPoints: A question where responders need to follow a long-lived connection for hours points to VPC Flow Logs, because firewall rules logging records a connection once when it is established.

A question about complete packet payloads for a third-party detection appliance points to Packet Mirroring with a collector behind an internal passthrough Network Load Balancer, one policy per region.

A question about top talkers by hour with SQL and no second copy of the logs points to a log bucket upgraded to Observability Analytics, with a linked BigQuery dataset only for people entitled to every field.

quiz.q: Incident responders suspect a compromised VM keeps one long-lived TCP connection open to an external server and transfers data over hours. Cloud NGFW firewall policy rules logging shows only one allow entry at the start. Which telemetry shows the ongoing transfer?
choices: Packet Mirroring to an IDS collector, because it is the only telemetry that records sampled flow volumes over time
A second logging toggle on the same rule, because it forces new entries for each packet in an active connection
Cloud Audit Logs Admin Activity entries, because they list each data transfer made by a running virtual machine
VPC Flow Logs, because they aggregate sampled packets per 5-tuple so a long connection yields entries throughout
quiz.explain: Rules logging records a connection when it is established, once for as long as packets keep moving, while flow logs aggregate sampled packets over each interval and so describe an ongoing flow. Mirroring captures full packets rather than sampled flow records, and audit logs record administrative actions, not network volume.

quiz.q: A forensics team created one Packet Mirroring policy to mirror web VMs in two regions of the same VPC network to a single collector group in one region. The policy is rejected. What is the correct design?
choices: Create one policy per region, each with its own collector group behind an internal passthrough load balancer
Create one policy that selects sources by network tag instead of by subnet, which removes the regional requirement
Move the collector to a different project so it can receive mirrored traffic from instances in both regions
Replace the policy with a VPC Flow Logs configuration, because only that feature can capture packet payloads
quiz.explain: All mirrored sources of a policy must be in the same project, VPC network and region, and the collector must be in that region, so two regions need two policies and two collectors. The selection method does not remove the regional limit, and flow logs do not capture payloads.

recap: Use rules logging to prove which rule decided, flow logs (with TCP connection logging for short probes) to follow traffic, Packet Mirroring and Cloud IDS for payload and threats, and Observability Analytics for SQL, minding field-level access.

title: Audit Logs and Detection: Cloud Audit Logs, Log Router Sinks, Evidence Protection and Security Command Center

concepts.heading: Audit Log Types and Who Can Read Them
concepts.body: Cloud Audit Logs has four types. Admin Activity records configuration and metadata changes and is always on. System Event is written by Google Cloud systems for changes not driven by a user, and it cannot be disabled. Policy Denied is written when a service denies access because of a security policy violation, and it is on by default; you may keep it out of storage with exclusion filters but cannot disable generation. Data Access records reads and writes of data and metadata and, except for BigQuery, is disabled by default. Its configuration is part of an IAM policy that lists per service the log types ADMIN_READ, DATA_READ and DATA_WRITE to record. A noisy nightly job running as one service account is handled with an exempted principal under that log type, a deliberate audit gap to document, not by weakening the configuration for everybody. Organization, folder and project configurations combine as a union, so a lower level can add but cannot switch off what a higher level enabled. Reading them is separate: Logs Viewer sees the _Required and _Default buckets except Data Access logs, and Private Logs Viewer adds those.

concepts.heading: Routing Logs: Sinks, Aggregated Sinks and Destinations
concepts.body: In the Log Router every sink in a resource evaluates an entry independently, and a sink sends it on when it matches the inclusion filter and none of the sink's own exclusion filters. An exclusion on the _Default sink therefore changes what that bucket stores but not what other sinks receive, and it does not stop the entry from being generated. Aggregated sinks at a folder or organization cover every present and future child. A non-intercepting aggregated sink copies entries and leaves child sinks alone, which suits a security copy. An intercepting one stops matching entries from reaching sinks in child resources, apart from the _Required sink, so application logs disappear from project _Default buckets while Admin Activity entries still appear. Choose the destination by purpose. Pub/Sub delivers continuously to an external SIEM, and an inclusion filter on audit logs keeps per-gigabyte licence cost down. Cloud Storage suits cheap seven-year retention that is read rarely, BigQuery suits SQL analysis, and log buckets keep entries searchable in Cloud Logging. The sink's writer identity needs a role on the destination, such as roles/storage.objectCreator on a bucket.

concepts.heading: Protecting Log Evidence
concepts.body: Logs are evidence about the people who operate workloads, so keep them away from those people. Copy audit logs with an aggregated sink at the organization or folder into a dedicated project that the security team controls. Retention on a log bucket ranges from 1 to 3650 days for a custom bucket and defaults to 30 days. Locking a bucket makes its retention period impossible to shorten and the bucket impossible to delete until every entry has fulfilled the retention. The lock is permanent, so choose the value carefully, and pair it with a project lien. A sink into a Cloud Storage bucket inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter needs an ingress rule for the sink's identity; for an aggregated sink the documented identity type is ANY_IDENTITY, and the fix is a narrow rule for storage.googleapis.com and the destination project. Log views, each with its own IAM policy, let one central bucket serve many teams; a bucket can have up to 30 views. Default resource settings can set a Cloud KMS key for new buckets in an organization or folder, and a bucket's location must match the key's location.

concepts.heading: Detection and Response with Security Command Center
concepts.body: Match the signal to the detector. Security Health Analytics checks resource configuration, such as a public bucket. Event Threat Detection reads Cloud Logging and Google Workspace logs for events, and each rule lists the log sources it needs: a rule built on IAM Data Access DATA_READ logs cannot detect those events until those logs are enabled. Virtual Machine Threat Detection finds potentially malicious applications such as cryptominers, and Container Threat Detection finds runtime attacks. The documentation describes Event Threat Detection as a Security Command Center Premium tier service. Muting hides acceptable findings while scanners keep running; dynamic mute rules apply to existing and new findings and can expire, a static rule takes precedence when both match, and Security Command Center recommends dynamic rules only. New findings can go to Pub/Sub in near real time with a filter such as state ACTIVE. For a break-glass account, route audit logs to a central project and use a log-based alert on its principal. In an incident, disable the key or account, preserve logs and disks, investigate, then recover; deleting the project erases evidence.

examPoints: A question where an auditor sees Admin Activity entries but no data reads points to Data Access logs being off or readable only with Private Logs Viewer, not to a missing sink.

A question that needs a tamper-resistant copy of audit logs outside workload administrators' control points to an organization aggregated sink into a dedicated project with a locked bucket and a project lien.
A question about a threat rule that never fires points to the log types the rule requires, such as IAM Data Access logs, being disabled.

quiz.q: A platform team creates an intercepting aggregated sink at the organization level that matches all entries from projects under one folder. Afterward, application logs vanish from the _Default buckets of those projects, while Admin Activity entries still appear. What explains this?
choices: An intercepting sink blocks matching entries from child sinks, except _Required, which still holds Admin Activity
Admin Activity logs are copied twice by every aggregated sink, so the application logs were removed to save space
The intercepting sink deleted entries from the _Default bucket because exclusion filters apply to existing entries
Data Access logs were disabled for the folder, and application logs are a subtype of Data Access logs
quiz.explain: An intercepting aggregated sink stops matching entries from reaching sinks in child resources, with the exception of the _Required sink, which always receives its entries. Application logs normally reach _Default through a child sink, so they stop arriving there. Exclusions do not delete stored entries, and application logs are not Data Access logs.

quiz.q: A SIEM is licensed per ingested gigabyte, and the security team needs near-real-time audit events from every project, including future ones, while investigators keep full logs. Which design fits?
choices: An organization sink to Cloud Storage with no filter, because batch files arrive faster than any streaming path
Per-project sinks to Pub/Sub that each team creates by hand, with no filter, so the SIEM sees every entry
An exclusion filter on the _Default sink for audit logs, so the SIEM reads the smaller bucket
An organization aggregated sink to Pub/Sub with an audit-log inclusion filter, and full copies kept in buckets
quiz.explain: An aggregated sink covers projects created later, Pub/Sub delivers continuously for near-real-time ingestion, and an inclusion filter keeps the licensed volume narrow. Full copies stay in buckets for investigation. Batch files add delay, manual per-project sinks miss new projects, and an exclusion on one sink does not change what other sinks receive.

recap: Know which audit logs are always on, route them with non-intercepting aggregated sinks to a locked central copy, send a filtered stream to the SIEM, and match each Security Command Center detector to the signal it actually reads.

title: Compliance Foundations: Shared Responsibility, Scoping, Mapping Controls and Assured Workloads

concepts.heading: Shared Responsibility Moves with the Service Model
concepts.body: Under the shared responsibility model, Google is always responsible for the underlying network and infrastructure, and customers always remain responsible for their access policies and data. In between, responsibility moves with the service type. For IaaS such as Compute Engine, the customer handles most controls, including guest OS patching and network configuration. For PaaS such as GKE and BigQuery, Google handles more, while the customer still owns application-level controls, IAM and data security. A function on Cloud Run functions is an example of serverless shifting infrastructure but not code: Google is responsible for the function platform, and the customer for application logic, third-party packages in the deployment artifact, secrets handling and invoker permissions. So when a critical vulnerability is announced in a bundled open-source library, patching it is the customer's job, and dependency scanning in the build pipeline helps. A leaked service account key is also on the customer side, because credentials are part of access policy, so the customer owns detection and response in its resources and prevention through disabled key creation and short-lived credentials.

concepts.heading: Scoping and Mapping Requirements to Controls
concepts.body: Scoping starts from the data. Identify where regulated data is stored, processed or transmitted, then trace connectivity and access paths such as Shared VPC, peering and VPN, IAM trust, service accounts and shared secrets or keys, and include components that can affect the security of those systems. Put the in-scope projects in a dedicated folder with organization policies, firewall segmentation and logging, so a smaller environment needs controls and evidence. As a common scoping practice, keep regulated and non-regulated work in separate projects, because everything that shares a project with regulated data is hard to argue out of scope. For a mixed estate with on-premises systems, Compute Engine, GKE and BigQuery, build a matrix with service, data flow, regulation control, owner (Google or customer) and evidence. On-premises systems are entirely the customer's, and the customer must consider how controls for different services interact, for example data in transit between them. A requirement for physical security of data centers is an inherited control: answer it with Google's reports and certifications from the Compliance resource center, and still evidence your own IAM, network rules, encryption choices, logging and VM patching.

concepts.heading: Assured Workloads Control Packages
concepts.body: Assured Workloads groups control packages by the assurance they give. Regional data boundaries enforce data residency, with optional personnel controls in the "and Support" variants. Regulatory data boundaries deploy certified controls tailored to a specific regulation. Sovereign Controls by Partners are operated by a partner who manages encryption keys, access justification and audits. Start from who must operate the control: a Swiss bank that wants a local partner to manage keys and judge access justifications needs the partner-operated family, since residency alone does not provide it. A plain data boundary such as Canada Data Boundary restricts where resources are stored and used, not which Google support personnel handle a case. The "and Support" variants are listed in the Premium pricing tier, plain data boundaries in the Free tier, and personnel controls rely on Assured Support for Assured Workloads, which is available with Enhanced Support or Premium Support. Key rules differ by package. CJIS, ITAR and IL5 mandate customer-managed encryption keys and a separate key management project. Other packages such as IL4 allow Google-managed keys, with CMEK, Cloud EKM and key import optional.

concepts.heading: Folders, Existing Projects and Violation Monitoring
concepts.body: Creating an Assured Workloads folder selects an organization, a location in the hierarchy and a control package. The organization cannot be changed later. If Access Transparency is not enabled on the organization, it is enabled automatically at folder creation, and projects created or moved into the folder are configured to use it. The folder applies an organization policy that restricts resource usage to the package's supported products and allowed locations. For a project that already exists, analyze it against the package, make the required changes and then move it into the folder, because moving does not repair a noncompliant resource. Monitoring is enabled automatically at folder creation and compares organization policy settings under the folder with the package; resource violation monitoring can be enabled on the folder. A violation is Unresolved, Resolved (remediated) or Exception (accepted with a business justification). By default the Legal category of Essential Contacts is emailed, so add the security team to that category to receive the same notices. Viewing violations needs a read role such as Assured Workloads Reader; adding an exception needs violations.update, included in the Assured Workloads Administrator and Editor roles.

examPoints: A question where a customer assumes a managed service removes their duty for bundled libraries, leaked keys or data access points to the customer side of shared responsibility.

A question about proving physical data center security to an auditor points to Google's reports from the Compliance resource center for the inherited control, combined with the customer's own evidence for what it configures.

A question that needs a local partner to hold keys and judge access justifications points to Sovereign Controls by Partners, since a data boundary, even with an "and Support" variant, only enforces residency and personnel limits.

quiz.q: A function on Cloud Run functions bundles an open-source library in which a critical vulnerability has just been announced. The business unit assumes Google patches it because the service is fully managed. Who is responsible, and what helps?
choices: Google, because it operates the runtime, so the customer only needs to wait for the next platform release to be applied
The customer, because bundled third-party packages are its code, and dependency scanning in the build pipeline helps
Neither party, because open-source libraries are outside the shared responsibility model and carry no duty
Google and the customer equally, because every library used in a managed function is patched automatically on both sides
quiz.explain: Serverless shifts the infrastructure and runtime to Google but not the code the customer ships, including the dependencies it bundles. Scanning in the build pipeline finds vulnerable libraries before deployment. Managed describes who operates the infrastructure and does not transfer responsibility for what you deploy.

quiz.q: A Swiss bank wants a local, trusted partner to manage its encryption keys, access justifications and audits, in addition to enforced data residency. Which Assured Workloads family fits?
choices: Regional data boundaries, because residency enforcement covers key management by a local operator as well
Sovereign Controls by Partners, because the partner manages keys, access justification and audits
Regulatory data boundaries, because named-regulation packages assign key management to a local firm
Any package with the Free tier, because the pricing tier decides who operates key management
quiz.explain: Sovereign Controls by Partners are operated and managed by a partner, who manages encryption keys, access justification and audits. Regional and regulatory data boundaries enforce location and personnel controls, and the pricing tier does not decide who operates keys.

recap: Google secures the infrastructure and you secure your access and data, so scope from regulated data, map each requirement to an inherited or customer control with evidence, and choose the Assured Workloads package by who must operate the control.

title: Provider Access and Evidence: Access Transparency, Access Approval, Residency and Audit Evidence

concepts.heading: Access Transparency Shows It, Access Approval Gates It
concepts.body: Access Transparency logs record the actions Google personnel take when accessing Customer Data. An entry holds the affected resource and action, the time, the reason for the action and information about the accessor: physical location, employing entity and job category. Cloud Audit Logs record what members of your organization did, Access Transparency logs record what Google personnel did, and together they cover both kinds of administrative access. Seeing an action does not mean the customer approved it. Approval is a separate product, Access Approval, which requires an authorized customer administrator to approve a request before the Google administrator gets access. Access Transparency must be enabled for the organization first, and then you enroll services and decide who may approve, using the Access Approval Approver role. Requests arrive by email or Pub/Sub, approvals carry an expiry that the approver chooses and can be revoked, and each approval is cryptographically signed. A request not approved within 14 days or before it expires is dismissed automatically, and access stays denied in the meantime, so approvers need a rota to avoid delaying a support case.

concepts.heading: Enrollment Scope and the Documented Exceptions
concepts.body: Access Approval requests consent only for access to Customer Data stored in the services you enroll. There are three options: all supported services regardless of launch stage, which is the default and also enrolls future services; only services in the GA launch stage, which also enrolls future GA services; or specific services. The supported services page labels each service GA or Preview, and Preview approval support may change in backward-incompatible ways and has no SLA, so a regulator that excludes Preview features should not rely on the default. The page also lists access that does not generate a request. For BigQuery, viewing query text, table names, dataset names and dataset access control lists might not generate Access Approval requests because that pathway gives read-only access to metadata, while viewing query results or table data still generates Access Transparency logs. There is one exception to explicit approval: to address time-sensitive outages, a request may be approved automatically and logged in an auto approved state. Auto-approval is automatically disabled for workloads deployed with EU Data Boundary with Access Justifications or Sovereign Controls by Partners.

concepts.heading: Combining the Controls with Assured Workloads and Key Access Justifications
concepts.body: Access Approval can be used with an Assured Workloads boundary but does not require one. When both are used, the Assured Workloads personnel access assurances apply before Access Approval is evaluated, and request parameters that do not match the boundary, such as a global location, are secondary to the workload configuration. Use Assured Workloads for the guaranteed personnel boundary, for example a package that restricts Google personnel to a specific country, and Access Approval for extra per-request consent on top. Key Access Justifications is a different layer. It directs Google systems to generate a justification code for each cryptographic operation involving enrolled keys, covering service-based and direct API access, and lets you set a policy on keys to view, approve or deny requests based on the code. For select external key management partners the policy can be enforced exclusively outside Google Cloud. Access Approval authorizes Google personnel requests, Access Transparency shows when Customer Data is accessed, and Key Access Justifications controls key use for at-rest Customer Data encrypted with a customer-managed key. Which features and key types are offered depends on the Assured Workloads control package.

concepts.heading: Residency Commitments and Audit Evidence
concepts.body: Data residency describes where data is stored at rest, and Google's commitments apply to Customer Data at rest for services that can be configured for data location. Customer Data does not include resource identifiers, attributes or other data labels, and Customer Data in use by the configured service is processed only within the country of the selected region or multi-region, or within the EU for a European Union region. Service Data, such as billing data, is stored as described in the geography and regions documentation. Do not promise legal teams that resource names, labels or billing records are bound to the chosen region. Evidence is assembled from several sources: Google's certifications and audit reports from the Compliance resource center for inherited controls, your own configuration exports and logs for customer controls, Assured Workloads violation details and exceptions with their justification, and Access Transparency and approval logs for provider access. No product alone satisfies a regulation, because the customer maps each requirement to a control and remains accountable to its own auditor.

examPoints: A question that asks who must consent before Google support reads customer data points to Access Approval, while one that asks for a record of what Google personnel did points to Access Transparency logs.

A question where approvers are unavailable and a support request sits unanswered points to access staying denied, with automatic dismissal after 14 days or at expiry, and to a rota and monitored notifications.

A question where a regulator wants no automatic approval of Google access, even during an outage, points to workloads deployed with EU Data Boundary with Access Justifications or Sovereign Controls by Partners.

quiz.q: A Google support engineer requests access to a customer's BigQuery data for a case under Access Approval, but the customer's approvers are on leave and nobody responds. A manager worries that the engineer will get access by default. What actually happens?
choices: Access is granted after a timer, because unanswered requests are treated as approved to avoid delaying the case
Access is granted through Access Transparency, which allows entry once the request has been logged and reviewed
Access stays denied, and the request is dismissed if not approved within 14 days or before it expires
Access is granted for read-only metadata, because every request for BigQuery metadata is approved at once
quiz.explain: Access Approval requires an authorized customer administrator to approve before access is given, and access continues to be denied if nobody answers. A request not approved within 14 days or before it expires is dismissed automatically. Access Transparency only records access, and automatic approval is limited to time-sensitive outages.

quiz.q: Legal states that residency obligations cover the customer's content and also billing records, resource names and labels. The engineer must explain what the Google Cloud residency commitments cover. What is correct?
choices: They cover Customer Data at rest, not resource identifiers or labels, and Service Data such as billing is separate
They cover every record, including billing data, resource names and labels, which are all bound to the selected region
They cover only data in transit between regions, because storage location is a choice the customer makes later
They cover resource names and labels, but not the content of objects, which is governed only by the encryption keys
quiz.explain: The commitments apply to Customer Data at rest for services configured for data location, and Customer Data does not include resource identifiers, attributes or labels. Service Data such as billing data is stored as described in the geography and regions documentation, so legal should not be promised that names, labels or billing records are region-bound.

recap: Access Transparency records provider access, Access Approval gates it per request with documented exceptions, Assured Workloads sets the baseline above it, and residency and evidence claims must stay within what the documents actually commit.

title: Final Review: Decision Cheat-Sheet Across the Five Domains and Test Day

concepts.heading: Test Day and the Identity and Access Cheat-Sheet (D1)
concepts.body: The Professional Cloud Security Engineer exam lasts 2 hours and has 50 to 60 multiple choice questions. The pass mark is not published. Configuring access is about 25%, boundary protection 22%, data protection 23%, operations 19% and compliance 11%. Read the last sentence, find the decisive constraint, and discard options that break it. Identity: with federation the IdP owns passwords and MFA, super admins bypass the IdP so protect them with Google 2-step verification. Service accounts: block key creation by organization policy, because Editor can mint keys, use short-lived credentials and impersonation, which logs both caller and service account, and use Workload Identity Federation for external workloads with an attribute condition and an immutable subject mapping. Authorization: Privileged Access Manager gives just-in-time, justified, audited grants with optional multi-party approval, deny policies with a tag condition apply one central guardrail, a Principal Access Boundary limits which resources principals can reach, and Access Context Manager defines access levels that VPC Service Controls, IAP and IAM Conditions enforce. Policy Analyzer answers who can access, Policy Troubleshooter answers why. Organization policy is set once on folders and inherited.

concepts.heading: Cheat-Sheet: Boundaries and Connectivity (D2)
concepts.body: Match the control to the layer. Cloud NGFW Essentials covers L3 and L4 rules, Standard adds FQDN objects and threat intelligence, and Enterprise adds intrusion prevention, URL filtering and TLS inspection, which needs a CA pool and client trust of the root. Cloud Armor protects at the edge: an edge security policy filters before the Cloud CDN cache, a rate-based ban throttles abusive clients, and new rules start in preview mode. IAP gates web apps by identity and context, and an SSL policy sets the minimum TLS version for client connections. Firewalls cannot tell which bucket an API call targets, so a VPC Service Controls perimeter encapsulates data at the API level; test changes in dry run and admit narrow flows with ingress or egress rules on identity, method and project, not broad IP levels. For private access to Google APIs from on premises, point DNS at the restricted VIP when VPC Service Controls must be honored, use a Private Service Connect endpoint for your own internal IP, and layer IPsec over MACsec, which protects only the hop to Google's edge.

concepts.heading: Cheat-Sheet: Data, Keys and AI (D3)
concepts.body: Sensitive Data Protection finds sensitive data with discovery and inspection, and de-identifies it: redaction and masking are irreversible, while AES-SIV and format-preserving encryption are reversible with a persistent Cloud KMS wrapped key. Restrict data access at the narrowest level: BigQuery roles on datasets, authorized views to separate who queries from who reads, public access prevention with domain restricted sharing for buckets, IAM database authentication for Cloud SQL, and Secret Manager instead of metadata for secrets, fetched with the VM's own service account. For keys, the default already encrypts, and CMEK adds control, audit and a revocation switch. Cloud HSM provides hardware protection, protection level is permanent, and Cloud EKM keeps key material outside Google at the cost of depending on the partner's availability. Rotation is only the first step, because data must be re-encrypted. Autokey keeps administrators who manage keys apart from developers who request them. Confidential Computing protects data in use and does not replace at-rest or transit encryption. For AI, only a VPC Service Controls perimeter denies out-of-perimeter access to Agent Platform APIs and data, and Model Armor screens prompts and responses for injection and sensitive data.

concepts.heading: Cheat-Sheet: Operations and Compliance (D4, D5)
concepts.body: Supply chain: On-Demand Scanning in Cloud Build gates a push, automatic scanning is detective, and Binary Authorization enforces attestations at deploy time, with dry run first and one attestor per approving team. Posture: custom constraints prevent, Security Health Analytics custom modules detect, and the security posture service deploys both and reports drift; policy changes are not retroactive. Logs: Admin Activity is always on, Data Access is off except for BigQuery, firewall rules logging records a connection once, flow logs follow ongoing traffic, Packet Mirroring gives payload, and Cloud IDS detects threats. Route with aggregated sinks, keep a locked central copy, send a filtered stream to the SIEM, and give auditors Private Logs Viewer for Data Access logs. Match Security Command Center detectors to signals, and mute rather than disable. Compliance: Google secures the infrastructure and you own access and data. Scope from regulated data, use the Compliance resource center for inherited controls, and choose the Assured Workloads package by who must operate the control. Access Transparency records Google access, Access Approval gates it, Key Access Justifications governs key use, and no product alone satisfies a regulation.

examPoints: A question that names a leaked or unneeded service account key points to blocking key creation by organization policy and moving to short-lived credentials, impersonation or Workload Identity Federation.
A question that stresses exfiltration through Google APIs, which firewalls cannot see, points to a VPC Service Controls perimeter, tested in dry run and opened with narrow ingress or egress rules.

A question that asks which control proves or limits provider access points to Access Transparency to record it, Access Approval to gate it and Assured Workloads to set the personnel baseline, while a regulation always still needs the customer's own evidence.

quiz.q: A company wants to stop developers from creating service account keys in every current and future project, and wants workloads outside Google Cloud to call APIs without any stored key. Which combination fits?
choices: An organization policy that blocks key creation, plus Workload Identity Federation with an attribute condition
An IAM deny policy that targets each developer, plus a shared key stored in Secret Manager for external workloads
A monthly key rotation reminder for owners, plus a firewall rule that blocks the external workloads' source ranges
A VPC Service Controls perimeter around every project, plus a longer lifetime for the keys external workloads use
quiz.explain: An organization policy applies to all current and future projects below it and developers cannot change it, and Workload Identity Federation lets external workloads exchange their own identity for short-lived access without a stored key, with an attribute condition limiting which identities are trusted. The other combinations keep keys alive or use controls that do not govern key creation.

quiz.q: A regulated bank needs evidence of what Google personnel did with its data, per-request consent before they can access it, and a guaranteed country restriction on that personnel. Which combination fits?
choices: Access Transparency alone, because logging each access also asks the customer's approver for consent before access
Cloud Audit Logs Data Access alone, because it records Google personnel actions and restricts their country
Access Transparency to record, Access Approval for consent, and an Assured Workloads package for the baseline
Key Access Justifications alone, because it replaces both the access record and the approval of personnel requests
quiz.explain: Access Transparency records what Google personnel did, Access Approval requires customer consent per request, and Assured Workloads personnel assurances set the baseline that applies before Access Approval is evaluated. Transparency does not gate access, audit logs record customer-side actions, and Key Access Justifications governs key use, not personnel access.

recap: Find the decisive constraint, prevent with organization policy and perimeters, detect with logs and posture findings, control keys and data at the narrowest scope, and in compliance remember that Google's reports cover only the inherited part.
